work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
label: The shut east gate
def: The outer east gate of the sanctuary in Ezekiel's vision, kept shut for ever because the Lord God of Israel has entered by it, and opened to no one else.
christ: The gate is the Virgin Mary: the Lord came into the world through her and left her a virgin still, as He later came in to the apostles through shut doors. She is "the east gate, spoken of by the prophet Ezekiel, always shut and always shining" (Jerome, *Ep.* 48.21).
where: Jerome, *Ep.* 48.21 — “She is the east gate, spoken of by the prophet Ezekiel, always shut and always shining, and either concealing or revealing the Holy of Holies”
Rufinus, *Symb.* 9 — “That Gate of Virginity was closed; through it the Lord God of Israel entered; through it He came forth from the Virgin's womb into this world”
Ambrose (quoted in Cassian, *Incarn.* 7.25) — “As is said in Ezekiel: "And the gate was shut and not opened, because the Lord passed through it." A splendid Virginity, and wondrous fruitfulness!”
Ps.-Methodius, *Sim. et Ann.* 10 — “the gate through which God appears in the flesh”
John of Damascus, *Exp. fid.* 4.14 — “He who was born preserved her virginity intact, only passing through her and keeping her closed”
